READABILITY.evidence: Names and doc comments are clear overall, e.g. decodeAllocChunk is well explained. But the edge-decode and point-decode logic uses single-letter locals such as `v := d.readUvarint()` and `n := d.readUvarint()`, plus `p`, `l` and `c`, which hits the single-letter cap.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: `func (s *ShapeIndex) decode` runs well over 100 lines, with header, shapes, cells and edges all inline. It also ignores the conventions: it adds a private `shapeIndexShapeKind` enum instead of the typeTag mechanism, and per-shape encode/decode is centralized in shapeindex_encode.go rather than lax_*.go/loop.go.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every count is bounded before allocating (maxEncodedVertices, numClipped <= len(shapes), numEdges <= shape.NumEdges()). Preallocation is capped at decodeAllocChunk. Shape IDs and edge IDs are range- and order-checked, and io.EOF maps to ErrUnexpectedEOF. A failed decode leaves the index unchanged, and nil or unsupported shapes return errors.

C7-14-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive: only the new shapeindex_encode.go and its test file are added. No existing typeTag values, per-shape wire formats or the Shape interface are modified.
